title: Collision event as a union of collision pieces
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $x, y \in \alpha$. Writing a hash function as a map $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the collision event on which $x$ and $y$ receive the same hash value decomposes as the union of collision pieces over all possible common values:
\[
  \{\, h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k \mid h(x) = h(y) \,\}
  \;=\; \bigcup_{a \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k} \{\, h \mid h(x) = a \text{ and } h(y) = a \,\}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: two points x, y of α
replaced:
For any $x, y : \alpha$ and any $k$,
\[
  \{h : \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k \mid h(x) = h(y)\}
  \;=\; \bigcup_{a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k} \texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a.
\]
